competency_fulfillment.rationale: The "counting up" framing is fulfilled in every item — seed 45 reads "Start at 82. Count up 5 more. What number do you land on?" and seed 47 "Start at 75. Count up 9 more. You land on ___". The qualifier "on the number line", which is what distinguishes this competency from a plain addition one, appears in only three of 17 samples: seed 43 "Show 64 + 7 on the number line.", seed 500 "Show 85 + 7 on the number line.", and seed 52 "The dot is at 52 and it moves forward 9 numbers." The other 14 use number-line-flavoured wording without ever showing or naming a line, so the representation the competency requires is mostly implied rather than illustrated.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The operand scope is well swept. Both sides of the decade boundary are exercised: non-crossing jumps at seed 42 (start 80, count up 3), seed 44 "Start at 15. Count up 2 more.", seed 601 (30 up 5) and seed 607 (66 up 1); crossing jumps at seed 46 (64 up 8 to 72), seed 47 (75 up 9 to 84), seed 52 (52 up 9 to 61), seed 600 (48 up 7 to 55) and seed 604 (36 up 7 to 43). The century boundary is reached once at seed 606, "Start at 98. Count up 2 more. What number do you land on?" (100). Starting points range from 15 to 98 and steps from 1 to 9, so the full 2-digit-plus-1-digit space is represented.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Structure fits Grade 2 Quarter 1. Stems are short and single-clause — seed 603 is just "Start at 20. Count up 1 more. You land on ___" — and the largest jump is 9 steps (seed 47), which is a countable number of hops for a second grader. The peer-check variant stays readable at this age: seed 604 gives "Carlo solved: "Start at 36. Count up 7 more. You land on ___". Carlo says the missing number is 43. Is Carlo correct?" No item demands multi-step planning or reading load beyond the grade.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: One template supplies essentially the whole batch. Seeds 44, 45, 46, 502, 601, 606 and 607 are the identical mcq sentence with numerals swapped ("Start at 90. Count up 2 more. What number do you land on?" versus "Start at 66. Count up 1 more. What number do you land on?"); seeds 47 and 603 are the same sentence in cloze form; seeds 68, 501 and 600 are the same sentence as a true/false assertion ("Start at 48. Count up 7 more. You land on 55. True or False?"); seeds 42 and 604 embed it inside a peer-check. That leaves only seeds 43, 500 and 52 with any different shape. No word problem, no object context, and no varied number-line presentation appears. The pair starting at 64 is also used twice, at seeds 43 and 46.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample is exactly 2-digit plus 1-digit addition described as counting up, with no drift past it: seed 46 (64 and 8), seed 501 (87 and 6), seed 500 (85 and 7). No subtraction, no 2-digit-plus-2-digit case, no regrouping vocabulary, and no algorithmic column language appears. Seed 606's result of 100 comes from "Start at 98. Count up 2 more.", which is still a 1-digit step and within the Grade 2 number range.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Magnitudes match the competency exactly. Every start is a 2-digit number, from 15 at seed 44 to 98 at seed 606, and every addend is a single digit, from 1 at seed 603 ("Start at 20. Count up 1 more.") to 9 at seed 47 ("Start at 75. Count up 9 more."). Results stay at or below 100, with seed 68's "Start at 95. Count up 4 more. You land on 99." and seed 502's 92 sitting near the top of the range without exceeding it.
